whyMe.title: Why me
whyMe.text1: I love turning an idea into something people actually use.
whyMe.text2: Before coding, I worked in social services and hospitality, so I know how much simple, clear interfaces matter. I work in a structured way, think analytically and keep going until a problem is solved, ideally as part of a team.

skills.title: My Skills
skills.learningText: My next goal is the backend. That is why I am learning Python with Django and the Django REST Framework and getting to grips with Linux.

projects.title: My Projects
projects.organisation: How I have organised my work process

dabubble.about: DABubble is a messenger inspired by Slack. Teams chat in channels, via direct messages and in threads, all in real time.
dabubble.organisation: I split the interface into reusable Angular components and bundled the data logic in services. Clear names and short functions keep the code readable for the whole team.
dabubble.teamwork: I built DABubble on my own, but organised it like a team project: every feature was developed in its own branch and merged into the main branch via pull request on GitHub, more than 40 pull requests in total. I worked in the feedback from my mentor review in separate fix branches.

join.about: The Join Issue Collector is a Kanban board with email automation. Anyone who sends an email to Join automatically gets a task in a dedicated board column via an n8n workflow, which a moderator then takes further. Guests can submit up to 10 requests per day, and with an account you can create, edit and drag and drop tasks.
join.organisation: Features are split into separate files by area (board, contacts, dashboard). Data is stored in Firebase, so changes are visible to everyone instantly.
join.teamwork: We built the original Join as a team of three and split the tasks on a Trello board. Building on it, I developed the Issue Collector with the n8n automation on my own and documented it so others can understand it and set it up themselves.

cuisine.about: Code à Cuisine suggests recipes based on the ingredients you have in your fridge. The suggestions are generated by AI.
cuisine.organisation: I built the project type-safe with TypeScript and encapsulated the AI request in its own module so it is easy to replace.
cuisine.teamwork: I built Code à Cuisine on my own. The frontend and the n8n workflows are clearly separated, so both parts can be developed further independently.

pollo.about: El Pollo Loco is a fun jump-and-run game: Pepe jumps over chickens, collects coins and bottles and finally faces the giant chicken.
pollo.organisation: The game is object-oriented: every character is its own class that inherits from shared base classes. A game loop updates and draws all objects on the HTML canvas, collisions are checked with bounding boxes (AABB), and state machines control movement and animations.
pollo.teamwork: I built El Pollo Loco on my own. Thanks to the clear class structure, new enemies or objects can be added without reworking existing code.

projects.linksSoon: Live test and GitHub will follow once the project is finished.

kanmind.about: KanMind is a project management tool with Kanban boards. The frontend was provided, I build the backend: a REST API that manages boards, tasks and comments and connects frontend and backend seamlessly.
kanmind.organisation: I plan the data models first, build the API with Django REST Framework in clearly separated apps and protect every endpoint with permissions. Tests accompany every new feature.
kanmind.teamwork: I am building this project on my own. I align the endpoints precisely with the given API documentation so that the existing frontend works without any changes.
